problem_text:
A municipality aims to formulate a stormwater runoff mitigation strategy to decrease total sediment load discharged from several industrial drainage outlets. Initially, no treatment measures are in place.

The characteristics of each outlet are as follows:
* For Outlet 1, sediment yield coefficient is 2.79, flow volume is 237.107.
* For Outlet 2, sediment yield coefficient is 2.406, flow volume is 124.728.
* For Outlet 3, sediment yield coefficient is 1.184, flow volume is 225.374.
* For Outlet 4, sediment yield coefficient is 2.909, flow volume is 265.177.
* For Outlet 5, sediment yield coefficient is 2.926, flow volume is 227.969.
* For Outlet 6, sediment yield coefficient is 1.632, flow volume is 283.878.
* For Outlet 7, sediment yield coefficient is 0.833, flow volume is 208.146.
* For Outlet 8, sediment yield coefficient is 1.532, flow volume is 100.222.
* For Outlet 9, sediment yield coefficient is 2.25, flow volume is 206.042.

To reduce sediment discharge, several filtration technologies can be installed, each with a specific capture efficiency:
* Technology1 captures 67% of sediment.
* Technology2 captures 62% of sediment.
* Technology3 captures 36% of sediment.
* Technology4 captures 12% of sediment.
* Technology5 captures 38% of sediment.
* Technology6 captures 13% of sediment.
* Technology7 captures 50% of sediment.
* Technology8 captures 34% of sediment.
* Technology9 captures 64% of sediment.

Implementing a technology at an outlet incurs an incremental cost per unit of flow volume. The cost matrix for all outlet–technology pairings is as follows:
| Outlet \ Technology | Technology1 | Technology2 | Technology3 | Technology4 | Technology5 | Technology6 | Technology7 | Technology8 | Technology9 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Outlet 1 | 31.927 | 76.925 | 101.27 | 118.421 | 136.76 | 89.321 | 152.095 | 169.864 | 64.326 |
| Outlet 2 | 170.987 | 163.578 | 109.319 | 14.802 | 37.612 | 137.348 | 47.981 | 152.535 | 40.578 |
| Outlet 3 | 64.457 | 57.607 | 169.483 | 141.213 | 66.077 | 153.183 | 16.138 | 164.665 | 29.471 |
| Outlet 4 | 174.927 | 150.504 | 174.32 | 151.058 | 116.641 | 55.143 | 159.018 | 161.776 | 64.651 |
| Outlet 5 | 136.254 | 186.032 | 83.635 | 191.773 | 195.406 | 69.404 | 114.904 | 12.463 | 57.755 |
| Outlet 6 | 127.907 | 158.376 | 175.322 | 167.697 | 183.182 | 143.88 | 133.05 | 153.47 | 113.857 |
| Outlet 7 | 124.644 | 157.468 | 193.215 | 65.894 | 43.711 | 139.705 | 45.526 | 43.021 | 107.631 |
| Outlet 8 | 81.668 | 91.416 | 115.754 | 34.713 | 120.957 | 58.453 | 72.807 | 144.841 | 39.413 |
| Outlet 9 | 39.204 | 71.3 | 19.663 | 187.153 | 126.966 | 135.759 | 103.205 | 118.809 | 78.036 |

The decision involves selecting which technologies to deploy at each outlet (outlets may employ multiple technologies concurrently), and an outlet may also remain partially untreated if needed.
The objective is to guarantee that the total sediment discharge is lowered by at least a proportion P = 0.592 of the baseline load, while minimizing the aggregate implementation cost.
